note: Fort Macleod Lions Club campground in the 20-acre John Zoeteman Park north of Fort Macleod on Hwy 811, along Willow Creek: rustic gravel-pad sites with fire pits and picnic tables, camp kitchens, public washrooms, a ball diamond and a playground. Updates are posted on the club's Facebook page. --Claude
summary: No operator page exists: the Lions Club has only a Facebook group and the Town of Fort Macleod's site does not list the campground or John Zoeteman Park. The local tourism site confirms 30 rustic/unserviced sites, first-come only, camp kitchens and washrooms. No rate, season dates, phone or maximum length is posted anywhere official; stored season (approximate, derived) left as it is.
flags: OWNERSHIP (stored local - not confirmed): the only non-aggregator page says 'the Fort Macleod Lions Club Campground sits in the 20 acre John Zoeteman Park' and does not say who owns the park. The Town of Fort Macleod's parks list (Centennial Park, Lioness Park, Puppy Love Dog Park, Community Gardens, River Valley Wilderness Park) does not include John Zoeteman Park or any campground, and the park is outside town on Hwy 811. No page read shows a municipality owning it; if the Lions Club owns the land itself this is `private` (a service club's own park), if the town or the MD of Willow Creek owns it and the club runs it, `local`. A web search found no page naming the owner. Nobody takes bookings: first-come only.

PRESENCE / RATE: no operator website (Facebook group https://www.facebook.com/groups/1136887220007557/ is what the tourism page links). Google Maps: 4.4 stars, 34 reviews, phone 403-715-8970, website field pointing at a hotel-booking page (hotelni.com). No official rate anywhere; Campendium (aggregator) shows a 2023 camper report of $20 - not written.
PHONE: stored 403-892-3560 is the number on Campendium; Google Maps shows 403-715-8970; neither appears on an operator or municipal page, so which is current is unverified.

WEBSITE: stored https://tourismfortmacleod.ca/stay answers 200 and is a tourism listing (GoDaddy site of the Cultural Heritage Tourism Alliance), the only page that describes the campground; no operator page exists to replace it.

WATERFRONT LEAD (stored not waterfront): the tourism page says the sites are 'along the banks of Willow Creek'. On Esri imagery (0.9 m/px) the loops sit in cottonwoods inside a creek bend; the creek is 15-20 m wide and the outer spurs on the south and east sides are roughly 30-60 m from the channel with trees between. Nothing shows open ground to the water; no change recommended (creekview at most if a view were shown).
SEASON: stored 05-01 to 09-30 'approximate' rests on old note prose; no official page gives dates (Campendium says May to Sept).
PIN: 49.75414,-113.40373 is at the west edge of the camping loops (loop centre about 49.7539,-113.4024, 95 m east); no move. Google's point (49.75652,-113.40601) is the Hwy 811 turn-off.
